hook.line: Some endings are so bad they almost become funny, and some performances are so good you run out of words. *Rozar* lets you say "it nearly gets there" in both directions.
hook.en: The ending borders on the ridiculous.

examples.en: The ending borders on the ridiculous.
The scene borders on the absurd.

rule:
*Rozar* really means "to brush against". For a verdict it says something comes very close to an extreme without quite crossing it.

It works for bad (*el ridículo, el disparate, la grosería*) and for good (*la perfección*).
There is no preposition: English "borders *on*", Spanish simply *roza el ridículo*.
The noun needs its article: *el ridículo, la perfección*. For an adjective idea, use *lo*: *lo absurdo*.
Put the verb in the tense you need: *roza* now, *rozó* for something finished.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a direct object that has no preposition: *rozar* takes its noun straight, with no *a* or *en*.

options: The ending borders on the ridiculous.
Her performance was far from perfection.
The scene borders on the absurd.
The set is far from perfect.
The play bordered on the ridiculous.
The play borders on the ridiculous.
Her answer borders on the absurd.
Your answer borders on the absurd.
Your answer bordered on the absurd.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El final roza ___ ridículo.* (*el* or *en el*) The ending borders on the ridiculous.
yourTurn.why: *Rozar* takes its noun directly, with no preposition.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Su actuación ___ la perfección.* (*rozó* or *roza*) Her performance bordered on perfection.
yourTurn.why: It is over, so use the past *rozó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The scene borders on the absurd.
Say: The set borders on perfection.
yourTurn.why: *Perfección* is a noun, so it takes *la*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: His speech bordered on rudeness.
Put it in the past: *El final roza el ridículo.*
yourTurn.why: Only the verb changes, from *roza* to *rozó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Her performance borders on perfection.
yourTurn.why: The same verb praises when the noun is good.

pitfalls.wrong: El final roza en el ridículo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "borders on", but *rozar* needs no preposition.
Almost. The noun keeps its article, *el*.
Almost. For an adjective used as an idea, add *lo*: *lo absurdo*.

personal: Think of a film, a meal or a plan that nearly went too far. Say it: *Roza…*.
